European Commission (2007). Integrated Pollution Prevention and Control: Reference Document on Best Available Techniques in the Production of Polymers (POL BREF), August 2007. European IPPC Bureau, Joint Research Centre, Seville. No DOI or report number printed.

Targeted pass of a 314-page BREF. Locators are PRINTED page numbers (PDF page = printed + 26). Loaded: whole-plant specific energy per tonne of polymer for every polymer chapter with numbers - LDPE, HDPE, LLDPE 1999 benchmark (APME 2002; European average and top-50 % average, total direct energy in kWh/t over all carriers, target blank), EVA copolymer, BAT-AEL direct energy for LDPE tube/autoclave, LDPE copolymer, HDPE and LLDPE new/existing; GPPS, HIPS, EPS (average and maximum); S-PVC and E-PVC thermal and electrical energy (Table 5.9) and an example S-PVC plant (electricity; steam in t/t in _flows); unsaturated polyester (current maximum, good practice, three plants, BAT) with on-site CO2 per tonne; ESBR and solution rubbers (steam and electricity); PA6/PA66 continuous and batch (Italy Table 9.3 and APME Tables 9.5-9.8 as separate processes); PET DMT/TPA/batch and solid-state post condensation; viscose staple and filament fibre (incl. BAT, mapped none); polyethylene plant economics (Table 3.14: total plant capital, derived capex per t/yr, non-feedstock variable and fixed cost for six PE routes, ChemSystems data); cogeneration efficiencies (Table 12.5, generic, reprinted from California Energy Commission 1982). Flows: about 1 t steam/t PP for the legacy slurry PP alcohol-wash recovery; example S-PVC steam 0.879 t/t. Other-values: quartile and primary-energy figures, full PE cost stacks, fibre spinning/processing energy (out of scope), devolatilisation extruder operating costs, LP-steam credit. Not loaded: PP (no data; the BREF says PP equals comparable PE processes), pollutant BAT-AELs, water, waste, noise, VOC-abatement and EMS costs; PS BAT tables 13.6-13.8 (repeat the European averages). Chapter 14 emerging techniques holds only a viscose H2SO4 recovery prototype with no energy figure. Chapter 12 techniques (cogeneration, reaction-heat steam recovery, gear pumps, online compounding) give no quantified energy saving, so there is no _measures file.

(1) Energy figures are total direct (delivered) energy with electricity and steam added at delivered value; a carrier split is printed only for PVC, ESBR and solution rubbers. (2) PE costs carry no explicit price year (ChemSystems 1996/97 for LDPE/LLDPE, 1999/2000 for HDPE; 1997 and 2000 assumed). (3) EVA Table 3.10 labels 1250 kWh/t "direct power consumption" while BAT Table 13.3 gives the level as direct energy 4.5 GJ/t. (4) PET TPA energy printed "2087 - 4500 (18500 1)" (footnote: high viscosity PET for food packaging). (5) UP plant 3 energy combines resin and gel coat. (6) Italy (Table 9.3) and APME (Table 9.6-9.8) PA ranges disagree for batch processes (PA6 batch 9500-10000 vs 4500-13500). (7) Typos: "Hazadous", "Polymeristaion", "comsummption".
